findings.title: Making `.small-action` a flex container disables its right-aligned action button
findings.body: The small-action row's action/undo button is positioned by the existing `float: right` rule, but a direct child of a flex container is a flex item and its float is ignored. Since neither the button nor `.small-action-desc` receives an auto margin or flex growth rule, the button will be laid out immediately after the description rather than at the right edge of the row. Replace the float-based positioning with flex positioning (for example, `margin-left: auto` on the button).

findings.title: The header panel is no longer right aligned in legacy WebKit flexbox
findings.body: The new flexbox mixin deliberately falls back to `display: -webkit-box` for Safari 6/older Android WebKit, but that 2009 flexbox implementation does not use `margin-left: auto` to consume main-axis free space. The previous `float: right` was removed, so in those browsers `.panel` is placed directly after the title/extra information instead of at the right side of the header, breaking the navigation layout. Provide a legacy-box-specific alignment fallback or retain a non-flex fallback for those browsers.

findings.title: The legacy Firefox flex fallback has no matching alignment declaration
findings.body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` enable the legacy `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box` layout, but `align-items()` emits only WebKit, MS, and unprefixed alignment properties. Firefox versions that select the `-moz-box` fallback ignore those properties, so the new centered header/small-action layout and baseline bullet-badge alignment fall back to stretch/default alignment. Emit `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside `-webkit-box-align`.
